name: MedBridge-RetrievalEval
description: Labelled retrieval queries over the curated MedBridge corpus (data/corpus_manifest.json). Mix of clinical and lay phrasing across all 13 manifest topics. Used by evaluation/retrieval_eval.py for Recall@5/@20, MRR and nDCG@5 of dense, sparse, hybrid and hybrid+rerank retrieval.
relevance_rule: A retrieved chunk is relevant to a labelled span when its guideline_id equals the span's guideline_id and its page range [page_number, page_end] overlaps one of the span's pages. For HTML sources a 'page' is the 1-based index of the h1-h3 section (virtual page) produced by medbridge.ingestion.html_parser.
label_method: Labels were found by regex search over the PARSED document text (medbridge.ingestion.parser.parse_document output, same page numbering as the index), never by running the MedBridge retriever, to avoid biasing the evaluation towards the system under test. Each span keeps the evidence_pattern that matched its page(s); every label is checked to match the parsed text and to be covered by at least one indexed chunk. Each query has 1-3 relevant spans; a query is answered if any span is retrieved.

queries.query: What blood pressure range defines stage 1 hypertension in adults?
queries.notes: BP category tables: stage 1 = 130-139 / 80-89 mm Hg.

queries.query: my blood pressure was 126 over 78 at the pharmacy, is that normal or high?
queries.notes: 120-129 systolic with <80 diastolic is the 'elevated' category.

queries.query: When should ambulatory blood pressure monitoring be offered to confirm a diagnosis of hypertension?

relevant.evidence_pattern: offer ambulatory blood pressure monitoring \(ABPM\) to confirm|135/85

queries.notes: NICE 1.2.3: clinic BP 140/90-180/120 -> offer ABPM to confirm; diagnosis thresholds 1.2.8.

queries.query: do I need more than one blood pressure reading before I'm told I have high blood pressure?

relevant.evidence_pattern: two or more readings at separate appointments
average of ≥2 careful readings obtained on ≥2 occasions
to confirm the diagnosis of hypertension

queries.notes: Diagnosis needs two or more readings on separate occasions (or out-of-office confirmation).

queries.query: What clinic blood pressure target does NICE recommend for treated adults under 80?

relevant.evidence_pattern: reduce clinic blood pressure to below 140/90

queries.notes: NICE 1.4.20: below 140/90 mmHg under 80; 150/90 at 80 and over.

queries.query: what should my blood pressure be once I'm on blood pressure tablets?

relevant.evidence_pattern: target blood pressure treatment goal of <140/90

queries.notes: Treatment goals: AHA/ACC <130/80; WHO <140/90 without comorbidities; NICE <140/90 under 80.

queries.query: How is resistant hypertension defined?
queries.notes: BP above goal despite >=3 drugs of different classes including a diuretic at optimal doses.

queries.query: my BP is still high even though I take three different blood pressure pills, what does that mean?
queries.notes: Lay phrasing of resistant hypertension.

queries.query: How is a hypertensive emergency defined?

relevant.evidence_pattern: A hypertensive emergency is the association

queries.notes: Severe BP elevation (>180/120 or >=180/110) with acute (hypertension-mediated) organ damage.

queries.query: Which intravenous drugs are recommended for hypertensive emergencies, e.g. labetalol or nicardipine?
queries.notes: Drug tables for IV treatment by type of emergency.

queries.query: How quickly should blood pressure be lowered in a hypertensive emergency without a compelling condition?

relevant.evidence_pattern: no more than 25% within the first hour|25% reduction in the first hour

queries.notes: AHA: reduce SBP by no more than 25% in the first hour, then <160/100 over 2-6 h; ESC: MAP reduction targets by condition.

queries.query: my blood pressure is 190 over 125 and I have a terrible headache and blurry vision, what should I do?

relevant.evidence_pattern: Hypertensive Crisis \(dangerously high blood pressure - seek medical care right away\)

queries.notes: Hypertensive crisis (>180/120): seek medical care immediately.

queries.query: How should severe hypertension without acute target organ damage (formerly hypertensive urgency) be managed?
queries.notes: No aggressive short-term lowering or parenteral therapy; reinstitute/intensify oral therapy.

queries.query: Which drugs treat severe hypertension in pregnancy in a critical care setting?
queries.notes: NICE 1.8: labetalol (oral/IV), oral nifedipine or IV hydralazine.

queries.query: what is heart failure? does it mean my heart has stopped?

relevant.evidence_pattern: doesn't mean that your heart has stopped

queries.notes: Heart can't pump enough blood; it does not mean the heart has stopped.

queries.query: What is first-line treatment for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction?
queries.notes: NICE 1.4.1: ACE inhibitor (or ARNI/ARB), beta-blocker, MRA and SGLT2 inhibitor.

queries.query: Should NT-proBNP be measured in people with suspected heart failure?
queries.notes: NICE 1.2.2: measure NT-proBNP; very high levels -> urgent referral.

queries.query: should I cut down on salt and drink less water if I have heart failure?

relevant.evidence_pattern: Do not routinely advise people with heart failure to restrict
Eating less sodium and drinking less liquid

queries.notes: NICE 1.9.10: do not routinely restrict sodium or fluid; MedlinePlus: less sodium/liquid in many plans.

queries.query: Which calcium-channel blockers should be avoided in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction?
queries.notes: NICE 1.4.12: avoid verapamil, diltiazem and short-acting dihydropyridines.

queries.query: what symptoms does heart failure cause, like swelling or getting out of breath?
queries.notes: Symptoms from reduced blood flow and fluid build-up.

queries.query: Which score is used to assess stroke risk in atrial fibrillation?
queries.notes: NICE 1.2.1: CHA2DS2-VASc; anticoagulate at score >=2.

queries.query: what is AFib and why does it put me at risk of a stroke?
queries.notes: AFib is an irregular heartbeat that can lead to stroke if untreated.

queries.query: Should a DOAC or warfarin be used for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation?

relevant.evidence_pattern: Offer anticoagulation with a direct‐acting oral anticoagulant

queries.notes: DOACs (apixaban, dabigatran, edoxaban, rivaroxaban) recommended over warfarin.

queries.query: is taking a baby aspirin enough to prevent a stroke if I have atrial fibrillation?

relevant.evidence_pattern: aspirin monotherapy for prevention of thromboembolic events is of no benefit

queries.notes: Aspirin monotherapy is not recommended / of no benefit for AF stroke prevention.

queries.query: What is the first-line rate control strategy in atrial fibrillation?

relevant.evidence_pattern: Offer rate control as the first‐line|digoxin monotherapy

queries.notes: Beta-blocker or rate-limiting CCB; digoxin in sedentary people.

queries.query: what treatments are there for AFib, do I need a blood thinner?
queries.notes: Blood thinners, rate/rhythm medicines, lifestyle changes.

queries.query: what are the warning signs of a heart attack?

relevant.evidence_pattern: symptoms of a heart attack|What are the symptoms of a heart attack

queries.notes: Symptoms of a heart attack; call 911.

queries.query: Which P2Y12 inhibitor should be used as part of dual antiplatelet therapy for NSTEMI?

relevant.evidence_pattern: as part of dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin

queries.notes: Prasugrel or ticagrelor with aspirin if angiography; ticagrelor when PCI not indicated.

queries.query: What drugs should be offered for secondary prevention after a myocardial infarction?

relevant.evidence_pattern: 1\.4\.1 For secondary prevention, offer people who have had MI

queries.notes: NICE 1.4.1: ACE inhibitor, dual antiplatelet therapy, beta-blocker, statin.

queries.query: Should everyone be offered cardiac rehabilitation after a heart attack?
queries.notes: NICE 1.8.1: offer cardiac rehabilitation to all regardless of age.

queries.query: Which antianginal medications are used first in chronic coronary disease?

relevant.evidence_pattern: antianginal medications, such as beta blockers

queries.notes: Beta blockers, calcium channel blockers or long-acting nitrates.

queries.query: Are SGLT2 inhibitors recommended for patients with chronic coronary disease?
queries.notes: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce MACE/HF outcomes; recommended in CCD with diabetes/HF.

queries.query: what is LDL cholesterol and why do people call it bad cholesterol?

relevant.evidence_pattern: What are HDL, LDL, and VLDL|LDL \(bad\) cholesterol

queries.notes: LDL is a lipoprotein; saturated fat raises LDL (bad) cholesterol.

queries.query: What statin intensity is recommended for patients with clinical ASCVD?

relevant.evidence_pattern: high-intensity statin therapy|High-intensity statin therapy typically lowers

queries.notes: High-intensity or maximally tolerated statin; >=50% LDL-C reduction.

queries.query: When should atorvastatin be offered for primary prevention of cardiovascular disease?

relevant.evidence_pattern: Offer atorvastatin 20 mg for the primary prevention

queries.notes: NICE 1.6.7: atorvastatin 20 mg if 10-year QRISK3 >= 10%.

queries.query: What LDL cholesterol level should be aimed for in secondary prevention of CVD?

relevant.evidence_pattern: aim for LDL cholesterol levels of 2\.0 mmol

queries.notes: NICE 1.7.1: LDL-C <= 2.0 mmol/L or non-HDL-C <= 2.6 mmol/L.

queries.query: my statin gives me muscle aches, what should I do?
queries.notes: Seek advice; measure creatine kinase; statin-associated side effects are mostly manageable.

queries.query: Should adults aged 40 to 75 with diabetes take a statin?

relevant.evidence_pattern: diabetes mellitus.{0,80}moderate-intensity statin|start with a moderate-intensity statin
moderate-intensity statin therapy is indicated for primary prevention in patients 40 to 75 years of age with diabetes

queries.notes: Moderate-intensity statin without calculating 10-year risk.

queries.query: What systolic blood pressure target is recommended for adults with CKD not on dialysis?
queries.notes: KDIGO 3.1.1: SBP <120 mm Hg when tolerated, with standardized office measurement.

queries.query: Should ACE inhibitors or ARBs be started in CKD with albuminuria?
queries.notes: KDIGO 3.2.1/3.2.2: start RASi for high BP + CKD with albuminuria.

queries.query: How much sodium should patients with CKD and high blood pressure eat?

relevant.evidence_pattern: sodium intake <2 g of sodium per day

queries.notes: KDIGO 2.1.1: <2 g sodium/day (<90 mmol, <5 g salt).

queries.query: can high blood pressure damage my kidneys?
queries.notes: Uncontrolled high BP can lead to (chronic) kidney disease / failure.

queries.query: Can an ACE inhibitor be combined with an ARB to treat hypertension?

relevant.evidence_pattern: Do not combine an ACE inhibitor with an ARB
combination of an ACE inhibitor and an ARB is not recommended
combined use of an ACEi and an ARB should be avoided

queries.notes: Dual RAS blockade is not recommended (harm).

queries.query: What is the step 1 antihypertensive for adults with type 2 diabetes?

relevant.evidence_pattern: do not have type 2 diabetes|adults with type 2 diabetes of any age should start on an angiotensin-converting enzyme

queries.notes: NICE: ACE inhibitor or ARB as step 1 for type 2 diabetes (CCB for >=55 without diabetes).

queries.query: I have type 2 diabetes, which blood pressure medicine is usually started first?

relevant.evidence_pattern: do not have type 2 diabetes|adults with type 2 diabetes of any age should start on an angiotensin-converting enzyme

queries.notes: Lay phrasing of step 1 treatment in type 2 diabetes.

queries.query: What is the first-line glucose-lowering drug in the WHO HEARTS diabetes protocol?

relevant.evidence_pattern: Metformin is recommended as the first-line|BEGIN METFORMIN

queries.notes: Metformin first line; sulfonylurea second line.

queries.query: Which antihypertensive is recommended first for chronic hypertension in pregnancy?

relevant.evidence_pattern: Consider labetalol to treat chronic hypertension in pregnant women

queries.notes: Labetalol; nifedipine if unsuitable; methyldopa as alternative.

queries.query: is it safe to keep taking my ACE inhibitor now that I'm pregnant?

relevant.evidence_pattern: Advise women who take angiotensin-converting enzyme|Stop antihypertensive treatment in women taking ACE inhibitors

queries.notes: Stop ACE inhibitors/ARBs within 2 working days of pregnancy notification and switch.

queries.query: Should pregnant women with chronic hypertension take aspirin to prevent pre-eclampsia?

relevant.evidence_pattern: aspirin 75 mg to 150 mg once daily from 12 weeks

queries.notes: Aspirin 75-150 mg daily from 12 weeks.

queries.query: What blood pressure target should be used when treating hypertension in pregnancy?

relevant.evidence_pattern: aim for a target blood pressure of 135/85

queries.notes: Target 135/85 mmHg.

queries.query: which blood pressure medicines can I take while breastfeeding?
queries.notes: Postnatal treatment incl. breastfeeding: enalapril, nifedipine/amlodipine, atenolol/labetalol; monitor babies.

queries.query: Which features of severe pre-eclampsia should prompt considering planned early birth?
queries.notes: Uncontrolled BP despite >=3 drug classes, falling platelets, impending eclampsia, etc.

queries.query: How should 10-year ASCVD risk be estimated in adults aged 40 to 75?
queries.notes: Use the pooled cohort equations (PCE).

queries.query: Should low-dose aspirin be used for primary prevention of cardiovascular disease?

relevant.evidence_pattern: Low-dose aspirin \(75-100 mg orally daily\) might be considered
Do not routinely offer aspirin for primary prevention

queries.notes: ACC/AHA IIb for select 40-70; NICE: do not routinely offer.

queries.query: what is the most important thing I can do to avoid heart disease?
queries.notes: Promote a healthy lifestyle throughout life (top take-home message).

queries.query: Which tool does NICE recommend to estimate 10-year cardiovascular risk?
queries.notes: QRISK3 for ages 25-84 without CVD.

queries.query: how much salt can I eat in a day if I have high blood pressure?

relevant.evidence_pattern: less than 5 g of salt per day
no more than 2300 mg of sodium

queries.notes: Less than 5 g salt/day (about a teaspoon); AHA: <=2300 mg sodium.

DASH combined with a low-salt eating plan

queries.query: does drinking alcohol raise my blood pressure?

queries.notes: Any alcohol associated with higher SBP; reduce or abstain.

queries.query: How much aerobic physical activity per week is recommended for adults?

queries.query: how can my doctor help me stop smoking?

relevant.evidence_pattern: 5As brief intervention to quit tobacco|benefits of quitting tobacco

queries.query: Which drug classes are recommended as first-line antihypertensive agents?

relevant.evidence_pattern: RECOMMENDATION ON DRUG CLASSES TO BE USED AS FIRST-LINE

queries.query: Should treatment start with a single-pill combination?

queries.query: What are white-coat hypertension and masked hypertension?

queries.notes: White-coat effect.
